- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates in the middle-to-late period after a spike, suggesting overshoot bias.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in upward trends.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model often predicts a sharp drop after a peak, but true price stays elevated longer.
- Forecasts show strong sensitivity to recent low prices, leading to premature correction or “panic” sell-off signals.
- When history includes a recent high, model often fails to capture the continuation of the trend, underestimating the peak’s persistence.
- In cases of sustained upward momentum, model underreacts to the trend, failing to anticipate the next peak.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–7 days, often missing the final surge or correction.
